reviews.review: A fun, although short game. First, the bad. The dialog isn't fantastic and the character development, well, isn't there. However, this is an intensely fun game that feels well-paced for its length. The atmosphere of the 40k universe is expertly folded in, with no barrels of exposition running your way.
This game is awesome. This is how Jesus felt when he punched the dinosaurs.

2/10
This game was 4 years in the making, and has that feel that if they'd had 6 more months they could have made something truly awesome
They didn't
Sadly, they didn't
It's a pity, because I really wanted to like this one, even if there was an Ultramarine, rather than any of the more interesting options (I sense the heavy hand of GW marketing there)
This game's single player campaign lasts areound 9 hours
2 of those hours are spent riding in lifts
another half hour is spent on cut scenes, leaving a short 3rd person shooter
Somehow, in that short time, it still manages to get repetitive, tedious and boring.
The designers went with the decision of making one model per enemy class, making about 20 different things to hit in total. When they attack in hordes of a half-dozen at a time, the lack of variety shows. When these same hordes attack in consecutive rooms for an hour, you give in to despair. Identical hordes charging headlong would have seemed OK if they were Tyranic, but Da Orkz is famous for their kustom jobz and variety.
This makes it feel cheap and rushed, which is a shame.

WARHAMMER 40,000 SPACE MARINE is true to the deepest black hole core to the legendary gaming series created by Games Workshop and all its video game conversions bringing the non-stop violent nightmare reality to a excellently executed third person point of view.

Grisly graphics, heart pounding tense audio effects, immersive voice acting, epic battle inspiring music, fun detailed game mechanics which are easy to get into yet have a surreal learning style to them such as using the very satisfying jump packs while trying to master manevouring while in flight all makes one feel like they are an actual Space Marine bringing the Emperors will to the enemies of mankind.

Enemies are varied and downright scary at times especially with the creepy sound effects.

Weapons and melee combat come with many easy to use combo moves which increase damage to a most brutally satisfying visual display. Truly gut wrenching euphoria.

Once more RELIC has dared as they did with WARHAMMER 40k DAWN OF WAR 2 and once again they have shown with jaw dropping success to the fan masses change is a good thing.

Here is hoping there will be many more chapters unfolding in the huge potential of SPACE MARINE. Praise the Emperor and purchase this violent strategic kill fest if killing Orcs and seeing little Gretchins run for their lives gets your blood going.

Thank you RELIC for always making your fantastic creations worth the price of admission :)
